title: Publish repository.bootstrap in the shared runtime contract and regenerate the client
description:
SPIDR child of task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9 (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05), which measured over the file cap. Independent of the engine child - no dependsOn.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AND WHY IT DETACHES CLEANLY. Publishing one command kind on this board costs 13 forced edits, five of them invisible to a grep for the kind literal. This row takes the SHARED-CONTRACT half only: `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` in packages/contracts plus the regenerated control-room client and its digest pins. The daemon-side half (vocabulary, registry, MCP fence, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS) stays in the parent.

THE SPLIT IS SAFE AND PRECEDENTED: apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-create-with-source.ts:35 documents that `goal.create_with_source` IS in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS but NOT in the daemon table. The shared contract and the daemon roster are deliberately NOT set-equal, so an intermediate HEAD where the kind is in the contract but not yet served is a landed, documented state - not a hole. Cite that file when anyone calls it one.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17 - these are the exact literals that must move, and they are the reason this is its own row:
- `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` (157 lines) holds RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.
- `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts:35` holds a HAND-TRANSCRIBED `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` array, asserted at :103, and a literal `expect(commands.size).toBe(104)` at :105. The file's own header explains a derived expectation would be vacuous, so the transcription must STAY transcribed - add the entry by hand, in sorted position, and bump 104 to 105.
- `git grep -ln GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` over source returns exactly six files: apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-collector.ts, apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-producers.test.ts, packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts, packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts, packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts, packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts. Re-census that grep yourself at HEAD before editing - the epic rail requires it across ALL file types, and two mirrors are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg.

NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client. Run the generator and quote the OLD and the NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST in the completion record.
definitionOfDone: `repository.bootstrap` is added to RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts with its payload shape (dir, productName, profileVersion, and the optional GitHub half: owner, name, visibility).

packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts is updated BY HAND: the entry is inserted in sorted position in the transcribed EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS at :35 and the literal count at :105 goes 104 -> 105. Do not replace the transcription with a derived expectation - the file's header explains why that would be vacuous.
The control-room client is REGENERATED, never hand-edited. Quote the exact generator command, and the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST values, in the completion record.

The four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors are re-censused at HEAD with a full-tree `git grep -n GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` across ALL file types (not just *.ts), the command and its file list are quoted, and every mirror carrying the old digest is updated. A mirror left stale is a rejection.

No daemon-side edit: daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-registry.ts, mcp-tool-allowlist.ts and agent-spawn-contract.ts are UNTOUCHED by this row - `git status --porcelain` proves it in the completion record.

taskRails: NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client: run the generator and quote the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST.
THE TRANSCRIBED ROSTER STAYS TRANSCRIBED. runtime-contract.test.ts:35 is hand-written on purpose; a derived expectation is vacuous. Edit it by hand and bump the literal count.
NO DAEMON-SIDE EDIT. Vocabulary, registry, MCP allowlist and HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS belong to parent task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9. Touching them here collides in the shared worktree.
RE-CENSUS THE DIGEST MIRRORS YOURSELF with a full-tree git grep across all file types; epicSiblings will not show you the rows that hold the precedent.

An intermediate HEAD where the kind is in the shared contract but not yet served by the daemon is a DOCUMENTED, landed state - see apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-create-with-source.ts:35. It is not a hole.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE THE THREE PREMISES THIS PLAN RESTS ON, and record each command with its output. Peers land rows continuously and every number below was measured at plan time.

1. `grep -n "repository.publish" packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` — confirms the insertion point (:109 at plan time). `"repository.bootstrap"` sorts BEFORE `"repository.publish"`.
2. `grep -n "commands.size).toBe(" packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts` — the literal to bump (104 at plan time, and the comment on the line above it says 102, which is already stale).
3. THE DIGEST CENSUS the epic rail demands, across ALL file types, not just *.ts:
   `git grep -n "GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST" -- . ":!.moe"`
   Quote the full file list. At plan time it showed exactly ONE literal — generated-client.ts:907 — with every other reference importing it. If a hand-transcribed digest has appeared since, it joins this row's owned paths; if not, say so explicitly rather than reporting a mirror sweep you did not need to do.

Also confirm `grep -n "repository.bootstrap" packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` returns NOTHING — if a peer has already published the kind, stop and report rather than landing a duplicate.

THE ROSTER ENTRY. In `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts`, insert `"repository.bootstrap"` into `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (:85) at its SORTED position — immediately before `"repository.publish"`.

That is the whole production edit. Do NOT add a payload type, a per-kind schema, or a branded interface: `packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts:37-39` states that no per-kind payload schema exists in the contract and that generating one "would invent a contract that does not exist". Payloads stay `JsonObject`. The payload KEYS for this kind are the parent row's `PAYLOAD_KEYS` edit in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9, its step 2) — see the row comment for why that satisfies this row's DoD item 1.

SORTED POSITION IS ENFORCED, not stylistic: runtime-contract.test.ts:117-125 asserts `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` equals its own sort, against the production tuple, precisely because a member inserted at the wrong position gets copied into the hand transcription and both stay green. Its comment names the incident. An insert anywhere else reds that arm.

THE HAND TRANSCRIPTION. In `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts`:

1. Insert `"repository.bootstrap"` into `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` (:35) at the SAME sorted position — before `"repository.publish"`.
2. Bump the literal at :105 from `expect(commands.size).toBe(104)` to `105`.
3. Fix the stale comment on :104: it reads "Literal 102" above an assertion of 104. Make the number match what the line asserts. Two numbers disagreeing on adjacent lines is how the next person mistrusts the arm.

DO NOT replace the transcription with a derived expectation. The file's header at :29-34 explains that `commands.size === RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.length` is the vacuous arm this transcription exists to replace: an expectation computed from the tuple under test can never fail. Hand-copy the entry; that deliberate edit IS the test.

CHECK THE OTHER TRANSCRIBED ROSTERS IN THE SAME FILE before moving on — :95-99 pin `RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS` and `RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_KINDS` by hand as well. This row adds a COMMAND kind, so neither should move; confirm that rather than assuming it.

REGENERATE THE CLIENT. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` (package.json:18 = `node --experimental-strip-types generator/generate.ts`). NEVER hand-edit `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts`.

Capture, for the completion record:
- the exact command;
- the OLD digest (`ed5f6b87cfca761b4389d66429046f5f2420f9fa04a373c1f22ab0608bfb8076` at plan time — read it from generated-client.ts:907 before regenerating, do not copy it from this plan);
- the NEW digest after regeneration.
A regeneration that leaves the digest UNCHANGED means the roster edit did not reach `canonicalContractSurface()` — that is a failure to investigate, not a pass. The generator emits the command section from a sorted copy of `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (generate.ts:289) and writes the digest at :264, so a changed roster must move the hash.

Then `git diff --stat packages/control-room-client/src/generated/` and confirm the ONLY changes are the new kind and the digest. A regenerated file carrying unrelated churn means the committed artifact was stale before you started — disclose that verbatim rather than absorbing it silently.

No edit is expected to `contract-pins.ts` (it re-exports) or `contract-digest.test.ts` (it derives the value with `deriveContractDigest()` and compares). If either needs one, the census in step 1 was wrong — stop and re-measure.

GATES (DoD 6). Run each leg standalone and quote its `Test Files N passed` count line — the OUTPUT, never the exit code. `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0; "No test files found" is also exit 0.

- `pnpm test` — the root lane, which is where packages/contracts and packages/control-room-client actually live (root vitest include covers `packages/**`). This IS valid evidence for this row, unlike a row touching apps/**.
- `pnpm typecheck`.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — required by the epic rail for any row touching the shared roster. Run it and quote the count line even though the step-1 census found no transcribed digest under apps/control-room: `vite.config.ts:30` aliases the generated client and :49 reads `pins.contractDigest`, so the app compiles against what this row regenerated.

STAY OUT OF THE DAEMON (DoD 5). Quote `git status --porcelain` and show that `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.ts` and `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts` are untouched. They belong to the parent row and a second edit here collides in the shared worktree.

REPO-WIDE BASELINE, path-attributed: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths. Completion needs that intersection EMPTY. Disclose any foreign red verbatim with its failing file paths.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW before `moe.complete_task`.

MUTATION DRILL — prove each arm you relied on is load-bearing. Every file in this row is TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` IS a valid restore proof here; `git status --porcelain` the paths first anyway.
- Move `"repository.bootstrap"` to a WRONG position in `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` and confirm the sortedness arm at runtime-contract.test.ts:117-125 goes RED. Restore. This is the arm the file's own comment says was added because a misplaced kind once passed both the tuple and its transcription.
- Remove the entry from `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` only and confirm the :103 equality arm reds. Restore.
- Leave the count at 104 and confirm :105 reds. Restore.
Record all three outcomes. An arm that has never been seen red is not evidence.

QUESTIONS TO ANSWER:
- Is `repository.bootstrap` now advertised anywhere it should not be? This row publishes it in the SHARED contract only. The daemon does not serve it yet, and the MCP fence lives on the daemon side — confirm this row added it to no allowlist, no affordance surface and no screen. `git grep -n "repository.bootstrap" -- apps packages` and read every hit.
- Is the intermediate state defensible? Cite `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-create-with-source.ts:35`, which documents an existing kind that is in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS and NOT in the daemon table. The two rosters are deliberately not set-equal. Put that citation in the completion record so the next reader does not file the gap as a defect.
- Does anything in the tree assert a COUNT over `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` that you have not updated? Search for hard-coded lengths beyond the one at :105: `git grep -n "RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS" -- packages apps tests tools` and check each consumer for a count or a transcription.
- Did the digest actually move, and did every importer follow? Re-run the step-1 census at HEAD and confirm no file still carries the OLD value.

comments.author: architect-fa3a3e17
comments.content:
DoD CLARIFICATION FROM MEASUREMENT (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05, filed before the plan). I wrote this row's DoD from the epic rail's description of the digest mirrors and from a shape I had not yet measured. Two of its clauses name things that do not exist at HEAD. Neither is narrowed — both are recorded here with what actually satisfies them, so QA grades against measured state.

1. DoD ITEM 1 says the kind is added "with its payload shape (dir, productName, profileVersion, and the optional GitHub half)". THERE IS NO PER-KIND PAYLOAD SCHEMA IN packages/contracts, and that is deliberate. `packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts:37-39` states it verbatim: "Payloads stay JsonObject. No per-kind payload schema exists in the contract, and generating per-kind payload types would invent a contract that does not exist." `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (runtime-vocabulary.ts:85) is a flat frozen tuple of kind STRINGS.
SATISFIED BY: the roster entry here, plus the `PAYLOAD_KEYS` entry in `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` — which belongs to the PARENT row task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9 and is planned as its step 2. Adding a per-kind payload type here would invent a contract the generator explicitly refuses to have, and would be a rejection, not compliance.

2. DoD ITEM 4 says "every mirror carrying the old digest is updated" and the epic rail says four mirrors, two under apps/control-room. RE-CENSUSED AT HEAD across all file types with `git grep -n GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST -- . ':!.moe'`: there is exactly ONE literal digest value in the tree —
  `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:907 = "ed5f6b87cfca761b4389d66429046f5f2420f9fa04a373c1f22ab0608bfb8076"`
— and every other reference IMPORTS it: contract-pins.ts:7 re-exports it, contract-digest.test.ts:21 DERIVES it via `deriveContractDigest()` and compares, v2-readiness-evidence-collector.ts:6 and v2-readiness-evidence-producers.test.ts:4 import it through `@moe/control-room-client/contract-pins`. `git grep` over `apps/control-room/**` for the digest returns ONLY `vite.config.ts`, which aliases the generated client path (:30) and reads `pins.contractDigest` (:49) — a build alias and a value read, not a transcribed digest.
SATISFIED BY: regenerating the client, which cascades to every importer automatically. The DoD's real requirement — re-census, quote the command and the file list — stands and is planned as its own step. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is still run per the epic rail.

3. INCIDENTAL, worth fixing while in the file: `runtime-contract.test.ts:104` carries the comment "Literal 102, not `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.length`" directly above `expect(commands.size).toBe(104)`. The comment's number is already stale at HEAD. Update it to match when bumping 104 -> 105; do not leave two numbers disagreeing on adjacent lines.

comments.author: architect-fa3a3e17
comments.content:
CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER COMMENT — point 2 was WRONG (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05). Read this before step 1; it changes this row's owned-path roster from 4 files to 7.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I censused with `git grep -n "GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST"` — the SYMBOL — and concluded there was one literal with every other reference importing it. Three of the four mirrors DO NOT MENTION THE SYMBOL AT ALL; they hard-code the hex. A symbol grep cannot see them. The epic rail says "a full-tree `git grep` of THE LITERAL across ALL file types" and it means exactly that.

THE CORRECT CENSUS, run at HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04):
  D=$(grep -o '"[0-9a-f]\{64\}"' packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts | head -1 | tr -d '"')
  git grep -n "$D" -- . ':!.moe' ':!.serena'
Digest at HEAD: ed5f6b87cfca761b4389d66429046f5f2420f9fa04a373c1f22ab0608bfb8076
FOUR HITS, exactly as the epic rail describes, two of them under apps/control-room:
- packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:907  (the generated source)
- packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts:36      (`const CONTRACT_DIGEST = "..."`)
- apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18
- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255            (a .tsx — a `*.ts`-only grep misses it)

CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS ROW:
1. Regenerating the client does NOT cascade to the three hand-transcribed mirrors. Each must be updated to the NEW hex by hand. My earlier "regeneration cascades to every importer automatically" is true only of contract-pins.ts, contract-digest.test.ts and the two cutover importers — not of these three.
2. The three added paths are OWNED by this row: `packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts`, `apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts`, `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx`. That is 7 distinct files, still under the 10-file cap, so no split is needed.
3. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` in the gates step is NOT a formality. apps/control-room is in none of `pnpm test` (root vitest include has no apps/**), `pnpm typecheck`, or the daemon leg — a forgotten mirror ships two hard-throwing tests behind three green gates. That is the precise failure the epic rail was written for.

The plan's step 1 already requires re-running the census across all file types and says any hand-transcribed digest found "joins this row's owned paths" — that instruction stands and now has a known answer. Points 1 and 3 of my earlier comment (no per-kind payload schema; the stale "Literal 102" comment) were measured directly and are unaffected.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
HAND-EDITING THE GENERATED CLIENT instead of regenerating. Rejected by task rail and by mechanics: the digest at generated-client.ts:907 is computed by the generator from `canonicalContractSurface()`, so a hand edit produces a digest that `contract-digest.test.ts:21` immediately contradicts — it derives the value independently and compares.

REPLACING THE TRANSCRIBED ROSTER WITH A DERIVED ONE while editing it. Rejected: the file's own header at :29-34 records that a derived expectation is exactly the vacuous arm this transcription replaced.

DOING THE DAEMON SIDE HERE TOO. Rejected — it is the parent row's plan (task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9, already submitted), and a second edit to daemon-command-vocabulary.ts from this row would collide in the shared worktree. This row proves it stayed out with `git status --porcelain`.

Size: 4 files, 6 steps. No split needed.
